children: InterGlobe Aviation Ltd (NSE:INDIGO) heads into Q2 FY27 results as fuel and inflationary cost pressures lift fuel CASK and ex‑fuel CASK, while forecasts see capacity and margins recovering through FY29 amid new ECB funding, aircraft deliveries with potential OEM delays, airport shifts and a Digi Yatra rollout.
: InterGlobe Aviation (INDIGO) reported fuel CASK of INR 2.44 (up 68.9% YoY) and ex‑fuel/ex‑forex CASK of INR 3.65 (up 13.7% YoY) due to higher ATF and inflationary cost pressures.
InterGlobe Aviation INDIGO Growth Outlook HOLD
: Analyst forecasts 11% ASKM CAGR for InterGlobe Aviation (INDIGO) FY26–FY29, FY27 FX‑adjusted EBITDAR margin 19.1%, rising to 25.0% in FY28 and 27.1% in FY29; rating: HOLD.
: InterGlobe Aviation (INDIGO) raised $180M in Aug 2026 via ECB special permission to finance capital goods imports, structured as an ECB with a leasing company lender.
: InterGlobe Aviation (INDIGO) says aircraft deliveries have begun but may face short-term OEM-related delays; company gave no details on number of jets or timing of delays.
: InterGlobe Aviation (INDIGO): Mumbai tariff order adds temporary 5 mppa traffic shift. All international traffic will return to CSMIA after T2 expansion. Redevelopment targets 65 mppa capacity.
: InterGlobe Aviation Ltd (INDIGO) will report Q2 FY27 results today; no figures or guidance were provided in the release.
: InterGlobe Aviation Ltd (INDIGO) joins Digi Yatra international beta from Nov 1 to Dec 2026 at seven Indian airports for overseas flights; wider rollout planned for 2027 pending feedback
